headline: Telecommunications Engineer Hopes 6G Will Finally Allow Him To Download His Father’s Unending WhatsApp ‘Good Morning’ Videos Instantly
body:
Q: With India joining the global push for 6G technology, what are the primary use cases you’re most excited about for the common citizen?

A: Look, forget the metaverse or remote surgery. My life’s ambition is to reach a bandwidth so high that my father’s daily 45-megabyte 'Good Morning' videos—the ones with the dancing marigold flowers and sitar music—start playing the millisecond he hits send.

Q: Are current 5G speeds not sufficient for those files?

A: It’s not just about speed, it’s about existential peace. Currently, there’s a three-second buffering lag. In that window, I have time to reflect on why he’s sending me a low-resolution clip of a sunrise when I am literally currently seeing the sun rise outside my own window. With 6G, the disruption is instant. It just loads and finishes before I can develop a philosophical objection.

Q: Do you think 6G networks will be implemented across the country in time to save your storage space?

A: I’m working with the standards board to lobby for a ‘Father-Filter’ protocol where the network automatically archives the videos into a deep-sea server in the Arctic, ensuring I never actually see them but he gets a ‘Delivered’ receipt. That’s the real promise of 6G.
caption: Forget the metaverse, the real 6G revolution is happening in the family group chat. How long until the 'Good Morning' videos load at the speed of light? #6G #TechNews #FamilyGroups #DigitalIndia (satire)
